tasks.label: FACTR: Launch grav-comp teleop + API (port 5000)
tasks.command: source /opt/ros/humble/setup.bash && source install/setup.bash; fuser -k 5000/tcp 2>/dev/null; sleep 1; /usr/bin/python3 -m src.factr_fastapi.factr_fastapi.factr_api & API_PID=$!; trap 'kill $API_PID 2>/dev/null' EXIT INT TERM; sleep 2; mkdir -p logs; : > logs/factr_health.log; /usr/bin/python3 -m src.factr_teleop.factr_teleop.factr_rizon_teleop 2> >(tee -a logs/factr_health.log >&2)
tasks.detail: WARNING: energizes the servos (torque ON, gravity comp). Put the leader arm in the calibration pose [0,0,0,1.57,0,0,0] (J4 ~90 deg, rest 0, gripper open) BEFORE running this task, otherwise factr_rizon_teleop blocks forever in _match_start_pos waiting for the arm to be posed. Frees port 5000 (fuser), starts the FastAPI server in the background (arm_index=0 -> left, port 5000) and records its PID, then runs factr_rizon_teleop in the FOREGROUND so its calibration/match prompts and live joint table are visible. On stop, a PID-based trap kills the background API (no pkill-by-name, which would self-match this task's own command line and spam 'Terminated'). Note factr_rizon_teleop has no clean-shutdown hook, so torque stays latched on the servos after stop (cut power to fully de-energize). If a previous teleop is still holding the serial bus, this run errors with a Dynamixel 'multiple access' message -- stop that process first. The teleop's stderr (all ROS logs incl. the per-second [health] servo telemetry and HARDWARE ERROR lines) is tee'd to FACTR_Teleop/logs/factr_health.log (created if missing, truncated each run; gitignored) AND still shown in the panel; watch it clean with 'tail -f logs/factr_health.log' since the 500 Hz screen-clear wipes the panel. Uses /usr/bin/python3 (3.10) since conda 3.13 can't load rclpy.
